scope: Proposition 9.9 (Capture by periodic quasiconvex groups) of the manuscript “Virtual compact specialness of hyperbolic one-relator groups” (preprints/Virtual-compact-specialness-of-hyperbolic-one-relator-groups-September-25-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 258 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 a6c45541e6943005), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 71. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Unless G is already virtually compact special by the acylindrical case, there is an invariant system of actual objects, finite modulo G, with full stabilizers A and kernels S = A ∩ L, having these properties: (i) h(A) ̸= 0; each A is quasiconvex, virtually compact special, and field-acyclic. (ii) Each S is a nested union of finite-rank free approximants of one constant rank at least two. Its field first-homology dimension is positive and finite, and its ambient homology detects every noncyclic subgroup. (iii) For representatives of the actual object orbits under L, the maps M H1(S; DL) −→ H1(L; DL) are jointly injective. Distinct actual object stabilizers intersect in at most cyclic groups. (iv) There is a uniform length such that the pointwise stabilizer of every longer noncyclically stabilized actual path, in T0 or in the refined tree T, is wholly contained in one of these kernels S.
